full_judgment:
3. Defendant No. 1 appellant contested the suit by filing a written statement. His case, in short was this. He took lease of the suit premises from Jana Jiban Dutta in 1952 and made constructions thereon. He recorded his name in the municipality and also in the PS Khatian. He denied relationship of landlord and monthly tenant between himself and the plaintiff or their vendor. Other non-contesting defendants are the tenants under the defendant No. 1. 

 6. There is no dispute as to Jana Jiban Dutra's ownership in the suit premises and that Kiran Bala succeeded him as his daughter. The disputed issue is whether the defendant-appellant took lease of the suit premises from Jana Jiban Dutta as alleged by him or he was a monthly tenant therein under Jana Jiban Dutta as alleged by the plaintiffs-respondents. High Court Division noticed that PS Khatian, Exhibit B, relating to the suit premises and exhibited by the defendant himself was recorded in the name of the plaintiffs' vendor Khairunnessa and in the remark column possession of the defendant was shown as trespasser since 1952. High Court Division further noticed that there was an agreement of monthly tenancy, Exhibit 14, between Jana Jiban Dutta and the defendant-appellant and that was misread by the trial Court. High Court Division also noticed that the lower appellate Court noticed the inconsistency of the defendant's claim inasmuch as he stated in a criminal case, Exhibit 12, that he took lease of the suit premises by a registered deed while in the written statement filed in the instant suit he alleged taking lease orally from Jana Kiran Dutta. While concurring with the finding of the lower appellate Court that the defendant executed a monthly tenancy agreement in favour of Jana Jiban Dutta on 24-7-52 which was proved by PW 2 Bijoy Chandra who was a grandson of Jana Jiban Dutta as Exhibit 14, learned Judge of the High Court Division himself compared the signature of the defendant-appellant appearing in Exhibit 14 with that appearing in the written statement of the defendant and came to the conclusion that both the signatures were of the same hand.
